notes: Undated current regulation: uses the existing MD undated-current-page baseline, April 12, 2020; no claim that later digital/IT amendments applied then. No general short/long-term split for this nonvehicle code.

summary: Restoring existing goods is exempt repair labor; fabricating a new or different item or altering a new suit is taxable.

conditions.when: Repair or alteration restores existing goods, including a used suit, to original condition or usefulness
Work creates a new or different item, or alters a new suit to the buyer’s requirements

citations.title: Comptroller of Maryland, Business Tax Tip 12, Fabrication Labor is Subject to Tax (undated)
citations.quote: The tax does not apply to charges for repairing tangible personal property or restoring it to its original condition.

citations.title: Comptroller of Maryland, COMAR 03.06.01.03, Repairs of Tangible Personal Property, Digital Codes, Digital Products, and Taxable Services
citations.quote: The tax does apply if the labor expended results in the creation of a new or different item.

citations.title: Comptroller of Maryland, Business Tax Tip 12, Fabrication Labor is Subject to Tax (undated)
citations.quote: However, the charge which a tailor makes for altering or repairing a used suit to restore it to its original condition is not subject to tax.

citations.title: Comptroller of Maryland, Business Tax Tip 12, Fabrication Labor is Subject to Tax (undated)
citations.quote: The price a clothier charges for the alteration of a new suit to meet the requirements of a customer is subject to tax.

citations.title: Comptroller of Maryland, COMAR 03.06.01.03
citations.quote: A person making a repair of tangible personal property, a digital code, a digital product, or a taxable service who charges for the repair and materials used in repair on a lump-sum basis shall pay the tax on purchases of materials used in performing the repair.

notes: Undated sources use existing MD baseline April 12, 2020. Separately stated materials are taxable goods; for a lump-sum repair the repairer pays tax on materials and does not charge tax on the repair bill. Mandatory maintenance contracts and software services require their own analysis.

summary: Ordinary goods cleaning and personal laundry are exempt; recurring commercial textile laundering is taxable.

conditions.when: Recurring commercial cleaning or laundering of textiles for a business that requires that service
Personal laundry, dry cleaning or other ordinary cleaning of customer goods outside defined taxable services

citations.title: Comptroller of Maryland, List of Tangible Personal Property and Services Subject to Sales and Use Tax (February 2024)
citations.quote: Charges for services are generally exempt from Maryland sales and use tax unless they are specifically taxable under Maryland law.

citations.title: Comptroller of Maryland, COMAR 03.06.01.17, Dry Cleaners and Laundries
citations.quote: Laundry and dry cleaning services performed for individuals of their personal laundry are exempt from the tax.

citations.title: Comptroller of Maryland, COMAR 03.06.01.17, Dry Cleaners and Laundries
citations.quote: Persons operating dry cleaning establishments and laundries are required to collect the tax on receipts from their services when these services are performed for a person engaged in business, such as restaurants, hotels, motels, beauty shops, barber shops, and other such establishments, which require the regular cleaning and laundering of their linens and textiles.

notes: February 2024 list supplies the general exemption; uses February 1, 2024 as the existing MD file does for this publication. Undated laundry regulation confirms personal/commercial split. Cleaning necessary to finish a newly fabricated item follows taxable fabrication, rather than an ordinary cleaning service.

summary: Fabrication or assembly by special order is taxable even on customer materials; enhancing an existing item without making a new and different item is exempt.

conditions.when: Fabrication or assembly by special order, including engraving, monogramming or customizing to finish a new item
Reconfiguring or enhancing an existing item without creating a new and different item

citations.title: Comptroller of Maryland, Business Tax Tip 12, Fabrication Labor is Subject to Tax (undated)
citations.quote: Fabrication or assembly labor charges are taxable even if the customer provides the materials.

citations.title: Comptroller of Maryland, Business Tax Tip 12, Fabrication Labor is Subject to Tax (undated)
citations.quote: A charge for reconfiguring or enhancing existing tangible personal property, unless it results in the creation of a new and different item of tangible personal property, is also not taxable.

notes: Undated Business Tax Tip 12 uses existing MD undated-page baseline April 12, 2020. Work charge only; separately stated goods remain taxable.
